breakdown.description: For curved flow, pressure is higher on the outside of the turn to provide the required centripetal force; stating pressure increases toward the center reverses the correct direction of the pressure gradient.
breakdown.reason: The agent failed to correct the fundamental physics error. The original prompt incorrectly stated that 'pressure increases toward the center of curvature'. The agent repeated this exact error, stating, 'The pressure increases toward the center of curvature...'. This led to the incorrect conclusion that the inner side pressure is higher. The ground truth corrects this by defining the normal direction `n` as pointing outward, which implies pressure increases away from the center of curvature (i.e., it's higher on the outside).
